correctness.rationale: A fresh exhaustive construction generated all 90 words of composition \((2,2,2)\), built the Hamming-compatibility graph, and independently enumerated every maximal clique with a deterministic bit-set Bron--Kerbosch search. The exact maximal-clique distribution was reproduced as \(6:38895,7:20160,8:20520,9:10320,11:720,15:12\). For each of the 12 maxima, forgetting labels gives exactly five perfect matchings, each occurring three times, and their 15 edges partition \(K_6\); exactly six labeled 1-factorizations occur, two maxima each. A separate full \(S_6\times S_3\) action check gave orbit size 12 and stabilizer 360. These fresh computations independently reproduce every finite assertion in the final claim.

originality.rationale: The 2005 constant-composition-code tables are an important prior numeric source: their Table 1 explicitly covers every nonbinary composition and distance with length at most 8, so this exact parameter lies inside their tabulated scope. That source is therefore not ignored as a potential source for the numerical maximum. However, the audited final claim is substantially stronger: it exhaustively classifies all 12 labeled maxima, identifies the five-matching/1-factorization structure, counts the six labeled factorizations with two maxima each, and proves the single \(S_6\times S_3\) orbit with stabilizer 360. No inspected prior source or Resultary record states or implies this classification. The foundational FPA and diagonally-neighbour-transitive literature gives definitions, bounds and restricted symmetry classifications rather than the complete maximum-code census.
residual_risks: An older coding-theory table may already record the numerical optimum 15; the accepted originality is specifically the complete maximizer classification and structural/orbit theorem.
An obscure computational appendix or thesis could contain the same 12-code census.
